answer:
**Irish ports that recorded between 10 000 and 100 000 passenger visits in **both** 2022 and 2023**

| Port | 2022 passenger visits | 2023 passenger visits | 2022 – 100 k? | 2023 – 100 k? |
|------|-----------------------|-----------------------|---------------|---------------|
| **Killybegs** | 11 146 | 27 910 | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Waterford** | 21 276 | 17 054 | ✓ | ✓ |

### How the numbers were obtained
The Central Statistics Office (CSO) publishes annual “Port Traffic” tables that include cruise‑ship visits and the associated passenger counts for each port.  
Table 6 of the CSO “Statistics of Port Traffic” release for 2022‑2023 lists both the 2022 and 2023 passenger totals for every Irish port that handled cruise ships:

> *Table 6: Number of cruise ships and passengers by port, 2022 – 2023*  
> …  
> **Killybegs** – 11,146 (2022) & 27,910 (2023)  
> **Waterford** – 21,276 (2022) & 17,054 (2023)  
> …  

(Excerpt from the CSO PDF – see **Table 6** in the 2023 release.)

Because both Killybegs (11 146 → 27 910) and Waterford (21 276 → 17 054) fell into the 10 000‑100 000 range for each of those two years, they are the only Irish ports meeting the criterion.

### Summary
- **Killybegs** – 2022: 11 146 passengers; 2023: 27 910 passengers  
- **Waterford** – 2022: 21 276 passengers; 2023: 17 054 passengers  

No other Irish port listed in the CSO’s passenger‑visit tables had figures between 10 000 and 100 000 for **both** 2022 and 2023.

### How the numbers were obtained
The Central Statistics Office (CSO) publishes annual “Port Traffic” tables that include cruise‑ship visits and the associated passenger counts for each port.  
Table 6 of the CSO “Statistics of Port Traffic” release for 2022‑2023 lists both the 2022 and 2023 passenger totals for every Irish port that handled cruise ships:

> *Table 6: Number of cruise ships and passengers by port, 2022 – 2023*  
> …  
> **Killybegs** – 11,146 (2022) & 27,910 (2023)  
> **Waterford** – 21,276 (2022) & 17,054 (2023)  
> …  

(Excerpt from the CSO PDF – see **Table 6** in the 2023 release.)

Because both Killybegs (11 146 → 27 910) and Waterford (21 276 → 17 054) fell into the 10 000‑100 000 range for each of those two years, they are the only Irish ports meeting the criterion.

### Summary
- **Killybegs** – 2022: 11 146 passengers; 2023: 27 910 passengers  
- **Waterford** – 2022: 21 276 passengers; 2023: 17 054 passengers  

No other Irish port listed in the CSO’s passenger‑visit tables had figures between 10 000 and 100 000 for **both** 2022 and 2023.
